reasons: The supplied paragraphs confirm the only proprietary-rights language is the Section 14(b) trademark clause and the Customer warranty at 9(c)(i) that it owns the Content and Properties; neither allocates ownership of deliverables, work product or Requests/visitor data, so 'missing' is the correct classification for this critical ip-data rule.

The inserted Section 13A is actionable and directionally correct: Customer retains Content, Properties and Customer Data; Kubient assigns Customer-specific deliverables; Kubient keeps the Auction Platform and background tools subject to a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, sublicensable licence-back; joint ownership is expressly excluded. This tracks the preferred position and creates no assignment of Customer IP/data to the Vendor.
Placement (new 13A after the Disclaimer, ahead of Section 14) and drafting style are consistent with the document, and the deterministic checks confirm no residual assignment to Kubient.
Comment is accurate, in-house voice, prefixed, explains the insertion in two sentences and offers the fallback licence, as the tone guidance requires.

Minor, non-fatal scope creep to note in negotiation: sub-clause (a) adds a use/disclosure restriction on Customer Data ('shall not sell, license or otherwise disclose ... except as reasonably necessary to provide the Services') that goes slightly beyond pure ownership and may overlap a confidentiality/data-use rule; also confirm 'Customer Data' is not already a defined term in Section 1 to avoid a definitional conflict.
